content: Standard-deviation-based outlier detection (z-score / N-std-dev-from-mean-or-median) is known to be weak on small samples — 3-std-dev methods rarely flag anything meaningful below roughly n=10-15. Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) with a modified z-score (cutoff ~3.5) is the more statistically robust alternative for small/skewed samples since it doesn't rely on the sample stdev being itself outlier-free. This is general statistical best practice, not project-specific verified guidance.
